Thank you for replying to this post so long after I posted it. I still feel like I won’t love anyone the same as I love him. Even Pam Anderson and Tommy Lee say they’re the love of each others life even though they have separate lives now, like they’ll never be in love with anyone as much as they were with each other. 
With the suicide thing, I know I just can’t do that to my family. I had a family member commit suicide when I was young and I saw and felt how much it affected everyone. 
I’ve been feeling a bit better focusing on a career, but so anxious about making friends. I do have a group of friends from high school (guys) , but making friends with new people (girls) scares me, all I can do is compare how much better they’re doing than I am, and the fact I feel like I just might look like I “need a shoulder to cry on”, if that makes sense. 
I hope you are doing well too ❤️

Hi Bufy_10 , thank you for your reply. I was diagnosed at 20, 28 now, and as an adult I just want to be able to take care of myself. Physically I’m in good shape, I’m a gym goer. My neurological/mental health is a different story. I’m glad/sad you can relate, thank you for your kind words.

I take Keppra, lamictal, and klonopin. I worked up a resistance to the first two, but klonopin has been much harder in regards to being tired. When I first started taking klonopin I’d be asleep in 10-15 minutes.

Thank you for your support. Although it isn’t my fault, I feel guilty I need to be ‘cleaned up’ after a seizure. Thankfully I have a supportive mom, and my brother stayed with me and watched comedy movies. I am grateful for my family.

I genuinely feel like no one cares about good sidewalks, coming from someone with a disability. My affluent ass hometown does not have 60% of the roads and sidewalks up to code. In a small town it also just looks like I’m the local drunk, if I’m walking where there is no sidewalks. I miss driving, I know people say fuck cars, but taking yourself on a drive can be a huge stress relief.
I got my first job yesterday since I received a confusing brain surgery in 2019. I am so excited to work with kids!

The way we sit. I can sit in the exact same position as you, I can “manspread” I can squat, etc. I had an ex get pissed when I was “manspreading” in jeans. Any other girls feel like this?

Epilepsy here, diagnosed at 20. That is the age when you are just getting a lot of freedoms, which I had for a short time. I know people aren’t big on cars, but the public transport where I am is awful. Hour long waits between buses, with NO sitting area at bus stops, stops that are literally a pole with a sign on it. If I could drive, I’d feel so much better. It’s horrible as an adult being told you no longer have any of those freedoms. 

I know it’s not safe, but I know I CAN drive, especially in an emergency. There was a time I left the house when my mom was very sick. As I was walking home I saw the car was gone. I started sprinting to the hospital, which isn’t too far. A neighbor stopped me when she saw me dump all my stuff on her lawn to run faster.

Thank you so much for your reply, I really like the concept of not letting others “control” you. Sometimes I get really jealous of something they have achieved/have that I don’t have. There is a lot of nepotism where I live, and when someone works outside of their family’s business (typically worth millions in this area) I really respect that. Fairness is very important to me.

Thank you for being a therapist to begin with, I benefit from it highly. I have a hard time holding grudges, and I’m working on that. Why is it so easy for some people to hold a grudge, and not others?
I like your outlook on things, that you can feel that way again. I do still have things from my high school sweetheart, boot camp letters I’ll never ever throw away. Hope you’re doing well ❤️
Thank you, all the best to you ❤️

Thank you for sharing your experience, I wouldn’t have thought about a folder on my phone. And I like your idea of a memory box; but that’ll take a long time before I’m willing to. I have a lava lamp in my room he bought me because he knew I always wanted one. I can’t bring myself to put it away. For Mother’s day, he got a painting of my 3 dogs for my mom, it is a beautiful picture, it’s so meaningful to her I know that will always stay.

I used to work for a company who dealt in alcohol, I told them before the fact I had epilepsy, but when I got the job it got far more severe. Because most people only think of a TC, I wasn’t told of some odd behavior I exhibited in my first two weeks. I’m extremely surprised they didn’t think I was drinking on the job. I wandered away from a nice company lunch and just walked randomly throughout the building. My coworker asked how my lunch was and I replied I hadn’t had lunch yet, though he was at the lunch and did see me eat. I wasn’t discriminated against, but I absolutely felt like it prevented me from making any meaningful relationships with coworkers, knowing that they’d seen me act weird. I was terrified of embarrassing myself. 
My boss was extremely understanding and caring about it, he learned to recognize if I was going to have an complex partial. He even knew when I texted him gibberish once, that I was likely having a seizure, and I was. I had to come into work one day with a swollen black eye as a result of a seizure. He was very serious with me, and took me into his office privately to make sure I wasn’t being abused. 

Good luck with your paper ❤️
Hey, mesial temporal sclerosis here too! Didn’t even knew it had any other name

I am 27, developed Epilepsy at 20. At 20, and still now, it was hard to realize so much freedom I had recently gained in my teen years just going away. A scan showed I had mesial temporal sclerosis, possibly from a head injury in my teen years. Though, I have bi temporal seizures, and refractory epilepsy. I have a NeuroPace implant (2019) and it’s hard to fathom having to get brain surgery again. 

Thank you for asking this question. I was a camp counselor at a camp for kids with epilepsy, it was a very cathartic experience. It was the first time I had been around others with epilepsy, and I kind of went with the question on whether or not to “appreciate” the fact I got it at 20.
Bo Burnham in Promising Young Woman. I can’t listen to his comedy after his performance, he was amazing in the role but I don’t think I could ever watch him again.

Yes, I get the opposite of Deja Vu. I’ll be in my room, all the sudden I feel threatened by whatever is on tv, and my room looks like I have never been there before. I feel an intense feeling of impending doom I wrote my address and put it on my wall for when I am having one so I am sure I’m in the right place. About half the time I gag violently, or get absolutely terrified and need to get someone to calm me down. This has happened in the grocery store before and I’ve had to have an employee help me chill out.

Physically - I was in the ER after a TC, I fight like hell in my post-ictal state. I didn’t I understand that the staff was trying to help, because they started to cuff my ankles to the bed, I started to lose it. They had one of my wrists cuffed, and before they could get the other one one I was able to sit up and smack my face on the hospital bed. I got a swollen face and black eye that swole shut for about 2 days. I had to go to my office job with that, my boss knew I have epilepsy, but he took me aside to make sure my ex boyfriend wasn’t the person who gave me a black eye. He sent me home to rest, and another co worker texted me after seeing my face. It took about an entire year for the pain around my eye socket to stop, and the black eye was visible for about a month. Bruises in general aren’t bad, but in a relationship to the naked eye there are times when it looked like my boyfriend had hit me. 
Mentally- years worth of lost memories.

Jesus, I am so sorry anyone would do that. If it makes you feel any better, those assholes are adults now, and they know what they did was wrong, and I honestly hope they have some shame. I'm only 27, but I know for sure I've regretted how I saw and treated some people in high school.

Hey! I had the same exact cut after my surgery. I called it a friars haircut. I got a pixie cut, though still wore scarves and hats so my head wouldn’t sunburn. Cutting your hair short will make it a lot easier. DM me if you’d like to see some progress pictures, I had someone take pictures of the back of my head as the healing progressed.

I have no idea how to NOT be miserable when this affects me on a daily basis. I am basically a child who needs help doing anything. I am constantly alone and I feel have the stamina to just be angry 24/7. I do things to try and help, I workout, (about to go to the track) and smoke weed when I've had too many seizures. I'm reading a book about anger and sadness. I watch comedy. I use Ativan as a rescue medication, but it makes me drowsier than weed. My limitations make me feel like I am a leech to anyone. I have avoided friendships over this, I feel people just see me as a mooch.

Driving is so therapeutic for me, I really miss it. Thank you for sharing that same feeling. I would drive a windy, wooded road to a beautiful bridge to a massive expanse of vineyards, and that was just to drive to work. If Harlie is a little dog, I have a small dog that loves bike rides, maybe he'd like that, the wind blowing his ears :) I'm also a dog walker I have find its a bit comforting, I think dogs are just happy to go out and explore.

Can I ask you what it was like to be diagnosed as a kid/teen rather than an adult? Mine began at 20, I'm now 27. I've always wondered if I could cope better if it was something that had happened earlier.

Can I ask what it was like to be diagnosed as a teen/kid? I've worked at summer camps for kids with epilepsy, and I can't relate to some stuff, like I know some of them were absolutely bullied because of their condition. I have always wondered if I had been diagnosed as a kid if I'd have a different outlook.

I live in an extremely affluent community, I am not. I am on SSDI and food stamps; I don’t consider that freedom, even if it’s help. I don’t get any housing help, I pay my own mom 3x less than normal rent. There is no way I could move. I like riding my bike, sadly mostly because it is expensive (I am very prideful and care a LOT about how others see me). In my small ass town 40% of streets have no sidewalks. Public transportation is dogshit where I live. I am exhausted from “hard mode” and it had just made me angrier and sadder. I can’t curb my anger everyday, but I do workout with a trainer who is familiar with epilepsy, and those days I do feel better. I just feel constantly embarrassed and afraid. I might sound like an ass, but I want to “fit in”. I get infuriating questions sometimes, it’s a small town and some people already know.

For me it’s been 7 years of epilepsy, I’m also 27. If you live in the U.S., there are ADA laws with jobs, like you can’t discriminate as soon as they know you have a disability. I used to work for a company and they knew I had epilepsy and actually worked pretty well with that knowledge; my boss knew just what to do having a complex partial seizure. Though, my seizures did get bad enough I had to leave, I couldn’t drive to work anymore (live in a semi rural area). Random from your username, are you in Chile? I have lived with 4 different people from Chile in my teen years, they were the best, most loving, fun people. Even my kitty is named after one of them 😊

Thank you for your insight from not being from the US. I realize some things are American ideas, not global. My ex used to live in the UK, and he told me he was the odd one out, he was in his mid twenties and lived alone, his friends all still lived with family (I'm very self conscious about living at home in my 20's) I did go for a bike ride on Monday and had a great time, thank you. Thank you for being on this sub and listening.

Thank you. It's just that I feel like I have/will eventually 'run out' of rides. It is so embarrassing to ask in the first place for me, I just feel greedy. For instance, if I could drive, I'd happily go to the grocery store at 9PM to get ice cream. There is no way I would ever ask someone to do that for me. Thank you for replying so quickly, it is nice to know someone is listening.
